2607.00601.title: "Don't Say It!": Constraints, Compliance, and Communication when Language Models Play Taboo
2607.00601.paper_summary: The game of Taboo requires describing a target word without using a set of forbidden words, so that other players can guess it. This deceptively simple task combines strict lexical constraints with the need for communicatively effective descriptions, making it a compelling playground for examining how LLMs navigate competing demands at inference time. We evaluate two open-weight models under conditions that intervene at progressively deeper levels of the generative process, from prompting to generation-time constraints to internal representations manipulations. We assess their outputs through forbidden word violation detection, LLM-as-a-judge measuring the degree to which generated descriptions successfully evoke the target concept for both human and machine guessers, and examining whether the strategies models adopt under constraint align with those of human players. Our results show that compliance with the rules of the game and communicative effectiveness trade off differently across conditions, and that models remain substantially weaker than humans as guessers, suggesting that lexical grounding under constraint is an open challenge for current language models.
2607.00601.paper_summary_zh: 這款禁忌遊戲要求在不使用一組禁止詞的情況下描述一個目標詞，以便其他玩家能夠猜出來。<lb/>這個看似簡單的任務結合了嚴格的詞彙限制和有效的溝通描述的需求，使其成為檢視大型語言模型（LLMs）如何在推理時應對競爭需求的引人入勝的遊樂場。<lb/>我們在逐步深入生成過程的條件下評估了兩個開放權重模型，從提示到生成時的限制，再到內部表示的操控。<lb/>我們通過禁止詞違規檢測來評估它們的輸出，LLM作為評判者測量生成描述成功喚起目標概念的程度，無論是對人類還是機器猜測者，並檢查模型在約束下採用的策略是否與人類玩家的策略一致。<lb/>我們的結果顯示，在不同條件下，遵守遊戲規則和溝通有效性之間的權衡有所不同，並且模型在猜測者的表現上仍然顯著弱於人類，這表明在約束下的詞彙基礎仍然是當前語言模型面臨的一個挑戰。
